prior_importants.description: The new under-lock recheck reads only the session's state. `pup retire` never changes state; it appends a `retired` event and leaves the session `merged`. So a `pup fix` that waited behind a `pup retire` passes every check and brings the retired branch back, which the ADR and the docblock say this change prevents.

`startFixRound` now always waits up to `MERGE_LOCK_WAIT_MS` (125 min). Its second caller, the web dashboard's `fix` action, is documented to refuse at once, so a page click on a held lock now hangs the request. It also stalls the dashboard's Ctrl-C shutdown for up to two hours.

findings.description: The new retired refusal always says a run held the merge lock meanwhile, but it also fires when nothing held the lock. Example: a session retired days ago whose PR was reopened on GitHub (retire deletes only the local branch), then `pup fix` with the lock free. The refusal itself is right, only the cause it names is false; wording it as "Session s1 has been retired (`pup retire`)" would cover both cases.
